blocks.text: Managing Zoom meetings on your Mac

As a technical account manager, you are often the bridge between product engineering and client success. Your meetings are frequent and technical. You cannot afford to fumble with settings while a client waits. Start by ensuring your macOS permissions are correct. Go to System Settings > Privacy & Security > Camera and ensure Zoom is enabled. Do the same for Microphone and Screen Recording. If you encounter a black screen when sharing, check these permissions first.
Essential Zoom keyboard shortcuts for Mac

Mouse clicks are slow and distracting. Use these shortcuts to keep your hands on the keyboard. To mute or unmute yourself, press ⌘ ⇧ A. To start or stop video, use ⌘ ⇧ V. If you need to share your screen quickly, use ⌘ ⇧ S. You can customize these in the Zoom app under Settings > Keyboard Shortcuts.

Technical glitches happen, even to the best managers. If your audio sounds like a fishbowl, it is likely the wrong input device. Click the arrow next to the mute icon and select your headset explicitly. Do not rely on the system default setting. If you are on an Intel-based Mac, keep your laptop plugged into power. Resource-intensive features like virtual backgrounds can trigger thermal throttling and stuttering on older hardware.
If you need to change your virtual background or blur your feed to hide a messy office, do it before the call starts. Use the Zoom settings menu to test your video output first.

blocks.text: Lazur lives in your Mac notch. It helps you keep your eyes on the client. If you forget where a setting is, hold ⌥ ⌘ and ask Lazur. Lazur will draw a circle around the button or guide you through the steps. This saves you from hunting through menus while your client is watching your screen.

Presenting data requires a clear screen. Hide your cursor if you are recording or presenting static slides to avoid distraction. Use the built-in Zoom tools to manage participants. Set up a waiting room to ensure only the right people join your sensitive account reviews. If you are sharing a video, remember to check the Share Sound box in the share dialog. This is a common mistake that leaves clients staring at a silent video.

Technical account managers spend a significant portion of their week in meetings. Use tools like Timing or Workspaces to track which client you are working for. After the meeting, use your dictated notes to update your CRM. If you use Lazur, you can dictate your meeting summary directly into your CRM or note-taking app. This creates a clean record without the manual typing delay.

items: Leaving your notifications on: Always use Focus mode on macOS to silence Slack and email pings.
Using the built-in microphone in a noisy room: Invest in a dedicated headset with noise cancellation.
Forgetting to record: Start the recording as soon as the meeting begins if you need it for later documentation.
Sharing your entire desktop: Share only the specific window you need to keep your private tabs or messages hidden.

faq.question: Can Lazur click buttons for me in Zoom?
faq.answer: No. Lazur does not click buttons or operate Zoom for you. It circles the button you need to click or guides you through the menu steps so you can do it yourself.

faq.question: Does Lazur work on Intel Macs?
faq.answer: Yes, Lazur works on both Apple silicon and Intel-based Macs running macOS.

faq.question: How do I fix a black screen when sharing my screen?
faq.answer: This is usually a permission issue. Go to System Settings > Privacy & Security > Screen Recording and ensure Zoom is toggled on. You may need to restart Zoom for the change to take effect.

faq.question: What is the best way to mute myself quickly?
faq.answer: The fastest way is to use the keyboard shortcut ⌘ ⇧ A. This works even when Zoom is not the active window.
